summary: Flucytosine (5-fluorocytosine, 5-FC) is an oral antifungal used in combination with amphotericin B or other antifungals to treat serious systemic Candida and Cryptococcus infections, especially cryptococcal meningitis. The usual dose is 50-150 mg/kg/day in four divided doses. It must be used in combination (never alone, to prevent resistance), the dose adjusted in renal impairment, and serum levels and blood counts monitored because high levels cause dose-dependent bone marrow suppression and hepatotoxicity.
indications: Serious systemic Candida infections (septicemia, endocarditis, urinary, pulmonary) in combination therapy
Cryptococcal infections including meningitis, in combination with amphotericin B

dosage.c: Systemic candidiasis / cryptococcosis (adult, normal renal function)
dosage.d: 50-150 mg/kg/day in 4 equally divided doses (every 6 hours)
dosage.n: Always combine with another antifungal; keep peak serum levels < 100 mcg/mL

dosage.d: 100 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses with amphotericin B
dosage.n: Part of standard combination induction regimen

dosage.d: Single dose then dose by serum level monitoring

admin: Take capsules orally; ingest a few capsules at a time over about 15 minutes to reduce nausea and vomiting
Always use in combination with another antifungal (e.g. amphotericin B) - never as monotherapy
Adjust the dose in renal impairment and dose after hemodialysis
Maintain regular dosing intervals (every 6 hours) and consistent timing
Monitor serum flucytosine concentrations to keep peak levels below ~100 mcg/mL
moa: Flucytosine enters fungal cells via cytosine permease and is deaminated by fungal cytosine deaminase to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). 5-FU is converted to 5-fluorodeoxyuridine monophosphate, which inhibits thymidylate synthase (blocking DNA synthesis), and to fluorinated RNA nucleotides that disrupt protein synthesis. Human cells lack significant cytosine deaminase, giving selectivity, though gut flora can convert some drug to 5-FU, contributing to marrow toxicity.

relative: Severe renal impairment (requires major dose adjustment and level monitoring)
Pre-existing bone marrow depression or hematologic disease
monitor: Patients on amphotericin B (nephrotoxicity raises flucytosine levels)
Elderly and those with reduced renal reserve

preg: Flucytosine is pregnancy category C and is teratogenic in animals; avoid in pregnancy unless the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether flucytosine is excreted in human milk; because of potential serious adverse effects, avoid breastfeeding or discontinue the drug.
renal: Flucytosine is excreted largely unchanged by the kidneys, so renal impairment markedly raises levels and toxicity risk. Reduce the dose and lengthen the dosing interval according to creatinine clearance, and ideally guide dosing by serum concentrations. It is removed by hemodialysis - give a dose after each session.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; flucytosine can cause hepatotoxicity (elevated enzymes, rarely hepatic necrosis). Monitor liver function during therapy.

major: Amphotericin B - synergistic antifungal effect but its nephrotoxicity reduces flucytosine clearance and raises levels/toxicity; monitor renal function and flucytosine levels
Myelosuppressive agents and radiation therapy - additive bone marrow toxicity
moderate: Cytosine arabinoside (cytarabine) - may inactivate the antifungal activity of flucytosine
Other nephrotoxic drugs - reduce flucytosine clearance
minor: No significant food-drug pharmacokinetic interactions of note
interactions.food: Taking capsules a few at a time over 15 minutes reduces GI upset; food does not require avoidance.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol due to potential additive hepatic and hematologic effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, and elevated hepatic enzymes, BUN and creatinine; can falsely elevate creatinine on some enzymatic assays.

serious: Bone marrow suppression - leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, pancytopenia (dose/level-dependent)

monitoring: Serum flucytosine concentrations - aim peak < 100 mcg/mL to limit toxicity
Complete blood count (and differential, platelets) frequently during therapy
Renal function (creatinine, BUN) at baseline and regularly, especially with amphotericin B
Liver function tests (transaminases, alkaline phosphatase) periodically
counsel: Take the capsules a few at a time over about 15 minutes to lessen nausea and vomiting
This drug is given with another antifungal and requires regular blood tests
Report fever, sore throat, unusual bruising or bleeding, or signs of infection (possible low blood counts)
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, severe diarrhea or abdominal pain
pk: Rapidly absorbed; antifungal action over days of combination therapy
Peak serum within 1-2 hours; target peak < 100 mcg/mL
Approximately 2.4-4.8 hours with normal renal function (prolonged in renal failure)
Store at controlled room temperature 15-30 C
pearls: Bone marrow toxicity is dose/level-dependent - keep peak serum flucytosine below ~100 mcg/mL and monitor CBC; toxicity rises sharply at higher levels
Always use in combination (classically with amphotericin B) - monotherapy rapidly selects resistance
Renally cleared - dose must be reduced in renal impairment and given after hemodialysis
Amphotericin B-induced nephrotoxicity raises flucytosine levels, compounding marrow toxicity - watch renal function and levels closely
Marrow suppression partly reflects gut-flora conversion of flucytosine to 5-fluorouracil
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered; if it is nearly time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed one and do not double up. Maintaining even spacing is important - contact the care team if multiple doses are missed.
overdose: Overdose risks severe bone marrow suppression, hepatotoxicity and renal effects. There is no specific antidote; treat supportively, monitor hematologic, hepatic and renal function for prolonged periods, and use hemodialysis to enhance elimination (flucytosine is dialyzable).
